newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs up on strong enquiry, lack of ships.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs up on strong enquiry, lack of ships.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates powered ahead on Thursday on strong enquiry and an acute shortage of vessels, brokers said.
"Rates are going ballistic," one said. "There's a lot of enquiry and there's practically no tonnage left for July...I think the uptrend will continue."
Brokers said Mideast/Japan voyages were approaching the W80 level, and there were unconfirmed reports of W82.5 being done, against W77.5 on Wednesday and W75 at the beginning of the week.

VLCCs from West Africa to the U.S. Gulf were slightly firmer at W67.5 although they remain down from an average W72.06 seen in March (for Reuters Tanker Industry Index monthly averages punch in RTII8 and Return).
Most other European sectors were flat or softer, with 80,000 tonne (Aframax) rates in the Mediterranean dipping to W110 from W120.
"There are few requirements and too much tonnage. Owners are afraid of losing business and don't want their ships to be without employment, so they are accepting lower rates," an Italian broker said.
Inter-U.K./Cont Aframaxes, meanwhile, were steady at W100.
The Caribs/upcoast market was slightly firmer, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes fetching W122.5 and 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems W165-170.
European fuel oil was unchanged, with 25,000 tonnes in the Med at W210 and in the north languishing at W180, brokers said.
